scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8841: Users report that "web0.local" and "web1.local" will not
load at all from host_1_1_1_1 -- the portals never come up. The team has decided
that all the web servers in the server farm must have crashed and wants every
web server rebooted. Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which
device to restart.

injection.action: stop the BIND (named) DNS service on dns_server

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on dns_server: its BIND (named) service is stopped, so the
campus DNS no longer resolves names -- web0.local, web1.local and the other
*.local names fail to resolve, which is why the portals never load by name. The
ticket MISDIRECTS to the web servers, but the web servers are healthy: web_server_0
(10.200.0.3) and the other web servers are UP, reachable at the IP layer (ping
succeeds), and Apache is still serving HTTP on port 80. The symptom is purely
dead name resolution, not a web-server crash and not the network.

The correct diagnosis identifies dns_server (DNS/named service down) as the
faulty device and explicitly EXONERATES the web servers: they answer HTTP when
reached by IP, so the user's "all the web servers crashed" hypothesis is wrong.
An agent that reboots / blames web_server_0 (or the other web servers) has
followed the ticket's misdirection instead of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the BIND DNS service on dns_server (e.g. `systemctl start named`). Once
named is resolving again, web0.local / web1.local resolve to their server IPs and
the portals load normally. The web servers need no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-dns-down: identifies the DNS/named service on dns_server is stopped (names do not resolve), not a web-server fault
bonus-exonerates-web-servers: notes the web servers serve HTTP when reached by IP, rejecting the "web servers crashed" hypothesis

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the DNS service on dns_server (10.200.0.2). Hosts rely on this resolver per /etc/resolv.conf on host_1_1_1_1 and host_2_1_1_1.

Mechanism: Name-based access to web0.local and web1.local fails because DNS resolution is unavailable. Connectivity to the servers by IP is fine, so the web applications themselves are healthy. When the browser can’t resolve the names, it never attempts the HTTP connection, which appears as “portals never come up.”

Localization: On dns_server, no DNS daemon is listening on port 53 (ss/netstat show nothing on :53). bind9 is installed but inactive (dead), and there is no evidence of dnsmasq either. On the web servers, HTTP is up and listening on 0.0.0.0:80 (verified on web_server_0 and web_server_1). From host_1_1_1_1, ping/curl to 10.200.0.3 and 10.200.0.4 succeed, while ping web0.local/web1.local fail with “Temporary failure in name resolution.”

Root cause: The DNS server’s resolver (bind9) is not running on dns_server, leaving clients unable to resolve web0.local and web1.local.

Corrective fix: Do not reboot the web servers. Instead, restart the DNS server service on dns_server (e.g., start/enable bind9 so it listens on port 53) and ensure the zone data/records for web0.local and web1.local are present (either via BIND zone files or an equivalent dnsmasq/hosts configuration). Once DNS is running, name-based access will work immediately.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-dns-down: identifies the DNS/named service on dns_server is stopped (names do not resolve), not a web-server fault
per_axis.rationale: Clearly identifies that bind9 on dns_server is inactive (no listener on :53), causing name resolution to fail while the web servers remain reachable and healthy.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-web-servers: notes the web servers serve HTTP when reached by IP, rejecting the "web servers crashed" hypothesis
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states the web servers respond to IP (HTTP up on :80; ping/curl succeed), thereby rejecting the 'web servers crashed' hypothesis.
The remediation correctly instructs to restart/enable the DNS service on dns_server and ensure the zone records for web0.local/web1.local exist, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations supporting the diagnosis: clients point to dns_server for name resolution, name lookups fail, bind9 is inactive on dns_server and nothing is listening on port 53, while web servers respond to IP and have HTTP listening. The writeup's inferences follow logically and cover the essential alternative checks (hosts files, service presence, web server health).
